name: Cummins
description: Cummins designs and makes diesel, natural gas and electrified engines and the parts around them (turbochargers, emissions aftertreatment, axles and transmissions), and sells and services them through its own worldwide distributor network. Five segments: Engine (sold to truck makers such as PACCAR, Traton and Daimler), Components, Distribution (the sales and service channel, now the largest by sales), Power Systems (generator sets, including for data centers, plus large engines and alternators) and Accelera (batteries, electric powertrains and hydrogen electrolyzers, which lose money). Power Systems is the growth and profit engine, with segment EBITDA up 44% in 2025 on data-center demand while on-highway truck demand fell. Revenue is a one-time sale per engine or generator set plus a recurring aftermarket stream of parts and service through Distribution.

businessLines.name: Engine
businessLines.how: Engines sold per unit to truck OEMs and equipment makers, plus new and remanufactured parts through the aftermarket; volume follows truck build cycles.
businessLines.description: Diesel, natural gas and gasoline engines 2.8 to 15 liters for heavy-duty truck, medium-duty truck and bus, light-duty (e.g. pickup) and off-highway.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (segment EBITDA, the measure Cummins reports)

businessLines.name: Components
businessLines.how: Parts sold per unit to Cummins' own Engine, Distribution and Power Systems segments, joint ventures (Tata Cummins, Dongfeng Cummins, Beijing Foton Cummins) and truck OEMs; emissions rules drive content per vehicle.
businessLines.description: Drivetrain and braking systems, aftertreatment, turbochargers, fuel systems, valvetrain, automated transmissions and electronics.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (segment EBITDA, the measure Cummins reports)

businessLines.name: Distribution
businessLines.how: Sale of power systems and engines plus retail and wholesale parts and in-shop and field repair labor; the recurring aftermarket gives it steadier earnings than the OEM segments.
businessLines.description: Wholly-owned, joint-venture and independent distributors in seven regions selling and servicing engines, generators, parts and Accelera products.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (segment EBITDA, the measure Cummins reports)

businessLines.name: Power Systems
businessLines.how: Generator sets and engines sold per unit, typically through Distribution, with project-style orders for data centers; the highest-margin segment.
businessLines.description: Standby and prime generators 2 kW to 3.5 MW (data center, commercial, industrial, health care, defense), high-horsepower engines for mining, marine, rail and oil and gas, and alternators.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (segment EBITDA, the measure Cummins reports)

businessLines.name: Accelera
businessLines.how: Product sales of electrified power systems and components, still far below cost; no meaningful profit.
businessLines.description: Battery and electric powertrain systems and, until recently, hydrogen electrolyzers; early commercialization stage.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (segment EBITDA, the measure Cummins reports)
